data.title: Journey Through Our Solar System
data.description: Explore four fascinating worlds in our solar system, learn their unique traits, and test your space knowledge!
data.introduction: Welcome, young space cadet, to an amazing voyage across our solar system! You will visit four incredible worlds, discover their special features, and prove your cosmic knowledge along the way.
data.celebration: Fantastic job, space explorer! You have successfully completed your journey and mastered the secrets of our solar system.

planets.description: Earth is our home and the only known world in the universe with liquid water on its surface. It is covered mostly by blue oceans and has a protective atmosphere filled with the air we breathe.
planets.funFact: Earth is the only planet in our solar system not named after a Greek or Roman god or goddess!
planets.transition: Now, let us travel to a much hotter and stormier world closer to the Sun.

questions.question: What covers most of Earth's surface?
questions.explanation: Earth is unique because liquid water covers most of its surface, giving it a blue appearance from space.

questions.question: How many moons does Earth orbit with?
questions.explanation: Earth has one natural moon that lights up our night sky.

planets.description: Mars is a cold, rocky world with a distinct reddish color caused by rusty iron in its soil. It features the biggest volcano in the entire solar system and deep canyons.
planets.funFact: Mars is home to Olympus Mons, a volcano that is three times taller than Mount Everest!
planets.transition: Next, let us zoom past the inner planets to visit the largest giant of them all.

questions.question: What gives Mars its reddish color?
questions.explanation: The soil on Mars contains lots of iron oxide, which is the same chemical compound as rust.

questions.question: How does the size of Mars compare to Earth?
options: It is the exact same size as Earth
It is much larger than Earth
questions.explanation: Mars is roughly half the size of Earth, making it a smaller rocky neighbor.

planets.description: Jupiter is the most massive planet in our solar system, made almost entirely of swirling gases. It features a giant storm called the Great Red Spot that has been raging for hundreds of years.
planets.funFact: Jupiter is so big that all the other planets in the solar system could fit inside it!
planets.transition: Finally, let us travel outward to visit the famous ringed world.

questions.question: What is Jupiter primarily made of?
questions.explanation: Jupiter is classified as a gas giant, meaning it does not have a solid surface like Earth.

questions.question: What is the famous feature known as the Great Red Spot on Jupiter?
questions.explanation: The Great Red Spot is a gigantic spinning storm in Jupiter's atmosphere larger than Earth itself.

planets.description: Saturn is a stunning gas giant encircled by massive, bright rings made of countless chunks of ice and rock. It is so light that if you could find a bathtub big enough, it would float in water!
planets.funFact: Saturn's rings are extremely wide, but they are surprisingly thin—like a piece of paper!

questions.question: What are Saturn's famous rings mostly made of?
questions.explanation: Saturn's dazzling rings are composed of billions of pieces of ice, dust, and rocky debris.

questions.question: How does Saturn's density compare to water according to fun space facts?
options: It is completely made of solid rock
It is denser than solid lead
It is as heavy as a mountain
It is light enough to float in water
questions.explanation: Saturn is made mostly of gas, making it less dense than water so it would float!

quizQuestions.question: Which planet has a distance from sun of 150 million km?
quizQuestions.explanation: Earth's distance from sun is 150 million km.

quizQuestions.question: Which planet has a distance from sun of 228 million km?
quizQuestions.explanation: Mars's distance from sun is 228 million km.

quizQuestions.question: Which planet has a distance from sun of 778 million km?
quizQuestions.explanation: Jupiter's distance from sun is 778 million km.

quizQuestions.question: Which planet has a distance from sun of 1.4 billion km?
quizQuestions.explanation: Saturn's distance from sun is 1.4 billion km.
